prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Reform UK Manifesto 2024 – Policy Summary (ideological framing removed)

Core pledges
- Freeze non-essential immigration; create a new Department of Immigration; tighten asylum rules; stop small boats and deport arrivals from safe countries.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at point of use; use independent capacity and tax incentives for staff and patients.
- Raise the personal income tax threshold to £20,000; cut energy levies and taxes to lower bills.
- Expand domestic energy from oil and gas; scrap Net Zero-related mandates and subsidies.

Immigration
- Freeze non-essential visas; exceptions for essential skills (notably health/care).
- Leave the ECHR; no illegal migrant resettlement in the UK; return small boats to France.
- Detain and rapidly process illegal arrivals, including offshore; bar asylum/citizenship for arrivals from safe countries; no legal aid for non-citizens.
- Immediate deportation of foreign offenders after sentences; potential citizenship withdrawal for serious crimes.
- Bar student dependents; close abuse of courses; 5-year residence/work for benefits.
- Employer immigration tax: raise NI to 20% for foreign workers (with exemptions); estimated £4bn pa revenue.
- Claimed savings: £5–10bn pa.

Government spending and regulation
- Stop paying interest on QE reserves to commercial banks (claimed £35bn pa saving).
- Cut 5% from non-frontline departmental spend and procurement inefficiencies (claimed £50bn pa).
- Halve foreign aid (save £6bn); collect more unpaid tax; repeal retained EU laws.

Tax and personal finance
- Lift income tax start point to £20,000; higher rate from £70,000.
- Reduce fuel duty by 20p/litre; scrap VAT and environmental levies on energy.
- Cut residential stamp duty (0% to £750k; 2% to £1.5m; 4% above).
- Reinstate VAT-free tourist shopping.
- Abolish inheritance tax for estates under £2m; 20% above.

Business and jobs
- No corporation tax for profits under £100k; main rate to 20%, then 15% (year 3).
- Abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high-street SMEs; 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals.
- Planning reform; deregulation, including easier hiring and firing; major tax simplification.

NHS
- Zero basic rate income tax for frontline NHS/social care staff for 3 years.
- End caps on medical training; student fee write-offs tied to NHS service.
- Expand use of independent providers (UK/overseas); 20% tax relief on private health and insurance.
- Patient vouchers if GP wait >3 days, consultant >3 weeks, operation >9 weeks.
- Efficiency measures (weekend theatres, fewer managers, contract reviews); public inquiry into excess deaths and vaccine harms.
- Cost: £17bn pa.

Public order and justice
- Recruit 40,000 police over 5 years; zero-tolerance approach; more stop/search.
- Mandatory life for drug trafficking; new “substantial possession” offence.
- Scrap DEI roles in policing; overhaul complaints system; more officers on the beat.
- Justice budget to £12bn; reopen magistrates’ courts; redefine hate crime; add 10,000 prison places.
- Costs: Policing £3bn pa; Justice £2bn pa.

Other sectors (highlights)
- Education: revise curricula for balance; prohibit gender identity measures in schools; 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap interest on student loans; longer repayment; tighter entry standards; expand PRUs; 2-year degrees.
- Benefits: tighter assessments; two-strike rule for job offers; return >1m to work; £15bn pa savings.
- Defence: spending to 2.5% GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay rises; Armed Forces Justice Bill; new veterans department; recruit 30,000; procurement reform. Cost: £14bn pa.
- Housing: fast-track brownfield; prioritize locals in social housing; restore mortgage interest deductibility for landlords; scrap Renters’ Reform Bill; leaseholder protections.
- Transport/utilities: scrap HS2 (one-off £25bn saved); ban ULEZ/CAZ/LTNs; regional road/rail upgrades; new 50/50 public–pension fund ownership model for utilities; cap standing charges. Claimed £5bn pa savings over first 5 years.
- Agriculture/fisheries: farming budget £3bn; end climate-linked farm subsidies; anti–price-fixing measures; “Buy British” targets; rebuild fishing fleet and processing; stricter control of UK waters. Costs: £2bn pa each.
- Pensions/social care: Royal Commission; single funding stream; curb offshore tax practices; review pensions; implement Mineworkers’ Pension recommendations.
- Constitutional/civil measures: leave ECHR; reform Human Rights Act, House of Lords, Civil Service and postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights; reform BBC and TV licence; new anti-corruption unit; oppose CBDC; review WHO links.

Funding summary (party estimates)
- Annual savings potential: ~£150bn pa plus £10bn pa from assumed extra growth = £160bn pa.
- Annual costs: ~£141bn pa.
